problems.title: New generation modules are not initialized as parameter copies
problems.source_location: Figure 2 and Section 3.2, PDF p.4; Appendix A, PDF p.17; submitted constructor and train_fsdp.py
claim: Figure 2, Section 3.2 and Appendix A specify copies of pretrained attention, MLP and normalization parameters. The constructor instead creates new modules after loading the base model.
analysis: `add_vision_attention` creates new linear projections; analogous MLP/norm methods create new state, while copy operations appear only in comments. A loaded four-dimensional query projection with every weight \(2\) and bias \(1\) maps the first basis vector to \((3,3,3,3)\); a newly initialized projection does not read those values. The fresh training path has no intervening copy pass. Inference and resumed training can separately load learned generation weights, which is a critical countercontrol.
result: The fresh recipe does not implement the stated copy initialization. It does not show that inference uses random generation weights or that original checkpoints began incorrectly.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Create independent copies of the intended loaded modules before optimizer creation, preserving equal initial values and distinct storage. Do not overwrite an explicitly loaded trained generation checkpoint with a fresh copy.
problems.impact_rationale: This is initialization correspondence in a public recipe, without demonstrated central original-experiment damage.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.
